question: A shopkeeper bought an article for ₹500. At what price (in ₹) should he sell the article to make 26% profit?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost Price (CP) is considered as the base value, which is 100%.

To make a profit of 26%, the Selling Price (SP) must be 100% + 26% = 126% of CP.

SP = 126% of 500

SP = 1.26 × 500 = 630

**∴ The correct answer is ₹630.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price of the article (CP) = ₹500

Desired Profit Percentage = 26%

**Formula Used:**

Profit = (Profit% ÷ 100) × CP

Selling Price (SP) = CP + Profit

 
 CP = ₹500
 (100%)
 
 
 SP = ₹630
 (126%)
 
 

 

 + 26% Profit

**Calculations:**

⇒ Profit = (26 ÷ 100) × 500

⇒ Profit = 26 × 5 = ₹130

⇒ Selling Price = CP + Profit

⇒ Selling Price = 500 + 130 = ₹630

**∴ The correct answer is ₹630.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Selling Price Formula

When the profit percentage is given, SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100.

Calculation for Loss

When a loss percentage is given, SP = CP × (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100.

Profit/Loss Base

Unless otherwise stated, profit and loss percentages are always calculated on the Cost Price (CP).
